output.summary: An herb native to tropical and subtropical Asia and Africa, Benghal dayflower has aerial, ground-level and underground branches bearing different flower types. Its roots and tubers are used as food; in Pakistan it is eaten as a vegetable, Nepalese people eat young leaves, and India records it as famine food.
